name: doc-ai-common
description: Shared Lambda Layer for Bedrock-assisted documentation semantic search (EmbeddingProvider, VectorStore, RetrievalStrategy). Consumed by the read-function and doc-indexer.
author: 63Klabs
//: >! RUNTIME/SECURITY NOTE: @aws-sdk/client-s3vectors and aws-xray-sdk-core are intentionally the bundled PRODUCTION dependencies. Per AGENTS.md the AWS SDK is normally provided by the Lambda runtime and must NOT be bundled (that is why the other @aws-sdk clients below stay in devDependencies, used only by tests). The S3 Vectors client is too new to be guaranteed present in the nodejs24.x runtime; vector-store-s3.js requires it at runtime on the DOC_AI_VECTOR_STORE=s3-vectors path, and the buildspec builds layers with `npm ci --omit=dev`, so leaving it in devDependencies would omit it from the deployed layer and crash the s3-vectors path at runtime. Bundling it here mirrors the s3-vectors-provisioner precedent. aws-xray-sdk-core is bundled for the same reason: the Lambda managed Node.js runtime does NOT provide it, xray-capture.js requires it at runtime to instrument the Bedrock/S3 Vectors clients (spec 0-0-6-xray-downstream-tracing), and a devDependencies placement would be silently omitted from the deployed layer, disabling X-Ray downstream subsegments without any error.
